incidents.victim: North American academic, medical, and military research community
incidents.vector: A China-nexus actor quietly compromised cross-sector research institutions and maintained covert access for over a year before discovery.
incidents.impact: Google Threat Intelligence found the intrusion targeting medical and research organizations went undetected for more than 12 months, exposing sensitive research data.

incidents.victim: Education sector organizations running Oracle PeopleSoft
incidents.vector: Attackers exploited Oracle PeopleSoft application infrastructure to gain access, steal data, and extort victims.
incidents.impact: Mandiant and Google identified an active compromise-and-extortion campaign against education-sector PeopleSoft deployments.

incidents.vector: A threat actor exploited a zero-day vulnerability in Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager to escalate from a compromised administrative account to root-level access.
incidents.impact: Mandiant reported active exploitation enabling full device takeover; affected organizations urged to patch and hunt for compromise.

incidents.vector: A malicious Chromium extension on a typosquatted domain impersonated Perplexity AI and used Manifest V3 rules to intercept every address-bar search query and keystroke before redirecting to legitimate search engines.
incidents.impact: Microsoft Threat Intelligence found the extension performing active surveillance of user search and keystroke input; it was reported to Google and removed.

incidents.victim: Edge, Chrome, and Firefox extension users (2.6M+ downloads)
incidents.vector: More than 119 malicious browser extensions across 90+ developer accounts offered genuine functionality, then deployed steganography-hidden payloads days after install to steal credentials and commit ad/search fraud.
incidents.impact: Over 2.6 million users downloaded the extensions; Microsoft removed 119 from the Edge store, with Chrome and Firefox variants also identified.

incidents.victim: U.S. and allied government officials, military personnel, and journalists
incidents.vector: Phishing posing as automated messaging-app support tricks high-value targets into surrendering verification codes, account PINs, and backup recovery keys for Signal and similar apps.
incidents.impact: FBI and CISA warned the ongoing campaign has compromised individual accounts and message histories of officials, military, and Ukraine-linked figures; stolen recovery keys persist even after account re-creation.

incidents.victim: Former U.S. National Security Advisor John Bolton
incidents.vector: An Iran-linked actor compromised Bolton's personal email account, which he had used to send classified national defense information.
incidents.impact: The actor exfiltrated top-secret U.S. government information; Bolton pleaded guilty to willfully retaining national defense information, facing up to 60 months in prison.

incidents.victim: Ukrainian government, military, and political organizations
incidents.vector: A Russian espionage operation deployed new malware against Ukrainian targets as part of its ongoing wartime cyber campaign.
incidents.impact: Researchers documented an expanded malware toolkit supporting sustained Russian cyber-espionage against Ukraine.

incidents.vector: Hacktivists defaced a public-facing Malaysian government web portal.
incidents.impact: The defacement protested planned internet age-verification laws; no data loss reported.

incidents.victim: Aflac Japan (Aflac Life Insurance Japan Ltd.)
incidents.vector: An unauthorized third party unlawfully accessed Aflac Japan systems over a roughly 10-day window in June 2026; the intrusion method has not been disclosed.
incidents.impact: Attackers accessed files containing policy details, personal information, and bank account data of Japanese policyholders; U.S. systems were unaffected and scope remains under investigation.

incidents.victim: Southeast Asian government and state-owned energy entities
incidents.vector: A Chinese-speaking actor exploited public web applications to deploy ASPX web shells, then used SoftEther VPN, Mimikatz, and a new TinyRCT backdoor for lateral movement and exfiltration.
incidents.impact: Unit 42 found a government entity and two state-owned energy firms compromised, with database and source-code theft; roughly 10 organizations were likely hit in a sustained regional espionage campaign.

incidents.vector: Attackers breached a third-party vendor and loaded malicious code onto the Polymarket website.
incidents.impact: Roughly $3 million was stolen before detection; Polymarket pledged to reimburse affected users.

incidents.vector: A cyberattack disrupted operations at a Russian dairy company; specific method not disclosed.
incidents.impact: Operations were disrupted as part of a string of attacks on Russian dairy producers.

incidents.vector: Attackers breached KDDI's public email service, which is shared with five other Japanese ISPs; intrusion vector not disclosed.
incidents.impact: Data of more than 14 million users was stolen.

incidents.vector: USB drives infected with Chinese malware were connected to classified military networks.
incidents.impact: Possible compromise of classified networks went undisclosed for nearly a year; Japan is now notifying NATO partners of a potential data leak.

incidents.vector: A ransomware attack struck an engineering and research subsidiary of the Indian automaker.
incidents.impact: Operations at one of India's largest automakers were disrupted; the incident was disclosed to market authorities.

incidents.vector: A cyberattack disrupted Ukrposhta's digital services; specific vector not disclosed.
incidents.impact: The operator's mobile app and some web services were knocked offline, with restoration ongoing.

incidents.vector: Data theft followed by extortion; the victim was listed on a leak site and allegedly stolen documents surfaced online.
incidents.impact: Tata confirmed a cyberattack after attackers claimed theft of 200,000+ documents, including data referencing Apple and Tesla components.

incidents.victim: Transport for London (and prior UK/US retail, hospitality, and healthcare victims)
incidents.vector: SIM-swapping, voice/SMS phishing, and social engineering stole employee credentials and bypassed multi-factor authentication to breach networks.
incidents.impact: Two UK members of a prolific cybercrime group pleaded guilty to the 2024 attack that crippled Transport for London, tied to 120 intrusions and at least $115M in ransoms; sentencing set for July 15, 2026.

incidents.victim: OpenClaw / ClawHub AI skill marketplace users (macOS, crypto holders)
incidents.vector: Malicious AI agent 'skills' on the ClawHub marketplace used Base64 curl-pipe-bash droppers and instruction hijacking to deliver macOS infostealers and exfiltrate crypto keys via Telegram.
incidents.impact: Unit 42 found five evasive malicious skills delivering infostealers and running agentic financial schemes, with command-and-control infrastructure still active; accounts were banned and skills removed.

incidents.victim: Klue and ~20 downstream customers (incl. LastPass, Snyk, Jamf, Tanium, BeyondTrust)
incidents.vector: Attackers used a compromised legacy integration credential to access Klue, then stole customer OAuth tokens and used them to download data from victims' Salesforce accounts.
incidents.impact: Roughly 20 companies — many of them security vendors — had Salesforce data stolen via compromised integrations; the attackers are extorting Klue and threatening to leak the data.

incidents.vector: Data was taken from a third-party company managing the agency's mobile device management platform, linked to a campaign exploiting Ivanti EPMM servers.
incidents.impact: Names, phone numbers, and email addresses of Belgian intelligence officials, plus mobile device details, were stolen.

incidents.vector: A network intrusion of undisclosed vector forced a full IT rebuild.
incidents.impact: The university is rebuilding its entire IT infrastructure following the hack.

incidents.vector: Attackers pre-deployed contracts weeks in advance, set up fake market opportunities, then drained the bot's funds.
incidents.impact: About $7.5 million was stolen from one of Ethereum's largest MEV trading bots.

incidents.vector: An intruder gained access to the national alert system and broadcast an unauthorized message.
incidents.impact: A fake extreme-level alert was pushed to phones across five regions including São Paulo, Rio de Janeiro, and Brasília; the government took the system offline.

incidents.victim: International cybercrime group (suspects detained in Ukraine)
incidents.vector: The group used ransomware and other schemes to extort individuals and companies across Europe and the US, laundering proceeds through real estate and assets in Ukraine.
incidents.impact: Four suspects were detained and $11.1M in assets seized (including $8.3M in crypto); the group's activity is estimated to have caused over $100M in losses.

incidents.victim: Fortinet FortiGate firewall and SSL VPN owners worldwide (incl. critical infrastructure and a NATO defense contractor)
incidents.vector: A global 'FortiBleed' campaign combined credential-stuffing and brute-force attacks with exploitation of older Fortinet flaws and a custom credential-sniffing script, then cracked harvested credentials offline to gain persistent admin and VPN access.
incidents.impact: Valid credentials for roughly 73,900 FortiGate devices across 194 countries were leaked and sold on Russian-language forums; attackers reached internal Active Directory environments and allegedly exfiltrated classified documents from a Turkish NATO defense contractor. ACSC and NCSC issued critical alerts urging credential rotation and device resets.

incidents.victim: Consumer Android TV streaming boxes (residential proxy abuse)
incidents.vector: Malware bundled on unofficial Android TV boxes conscripts the devices into a residential proxy botnet.
incidents.impact: A botnet of millions of devices has for years relayed traffic tied to ad fraud, account takeovers, and mass data-scraping; researchers linked the infrastructure to a commercial proxy provider that disputes the findings.

incidents.vector: A cyberattack struck Iranian banking infrastructure; specific vector not disclosed.
incidents.impact: Iranian banks were crippled earlier in the month; intelligence sources believe Israeli operators were likely responsible.
